paper.title: Every Microsecond Matters: Achieving Near Speed-of-Light Latency in GPU Collectives
adapted_lessons: Keep small decode collectives on the native latency path.
Select bandwidth-oriented compression only above a measured payload crossover.
Avoid barriers, communicator discovery, and diagnostic bookkeeping on the critical path.
paper.not_ported: The paper's LL/sentinel/symmetric-memory kernels target NCCL device APIs and NVLink-scale-up systems; this host is four PCIe SM120 GPUs using PyNCCL, with symmetric-memory/custom-allreduce paths unavailable.

environment.device: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

protocol.timing: CUDA events around model forward plus logits; rank-max; wall time around end-to-end generation

implementation: Large contiguous BF16 reductions use the existing FP8 E4M3 compressed collective.
Sub-threshold reductions return directly to vLLM's native all-reduce entry point before communicator/capability/policy work.
Feature configuration and threshold are cached once per worker process.
Diagnostic counters are opt-in and disabled for performance runs.
Native fuse_allreduce_rms was isolated but not selected because it added decode latency on this workload.

correctness: The bypass is stock all-reduce for every sub-threshold decode tensor. Large-payload FP8 correctness remains covered by the isolated A/B: model-sample max absolute error 1.01327896e-06; native RMSNorm fusion was separately exact on the captured 256-logit sample.
